assessment: Two unvalidated conversions. The observations establish selection, interpretation and insertion difficulties, but not their causes. Neither alternative yet demonstrates the pilot targets or feasibility within the fixed delivery date and cost caps.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: turn configuration differences into a visual completeness signal using reusable order-specific bench stencils with one outlined position per required component. A missing or mismatched part leaves a visible discrepancy; corresponding position labels on the existing customer diagram guide placement.
openings.delta: Uses variation and selection mistakes to generate checking information. Trial packing the checked components unassembled could remove workshop insertion time while retaining customer rearrangeability.
openings.prediction: Compared with ordinary order-slip checks, stencils detect more deliberately seeded missing or incorrect parts; matched customer labels reduce questions about short partitions.
openings.probe: Counterbalance stencil and ordinary checking trials across workers and layouts; separately time selection, checking and packing. Record seeded-error detection. Test labeled kits with the ten participants, then evaluate all success measures in the 60-unit pilot if feasible.
assumptions: Failure boundary: visually identical but functionally different parts evade outlines unless separately marked.
Customer assembly effort must remain compatible with the unaided-success target.
Template preparation, labeling and any packing changes must meet both cost caps and the fixed date; preserve ordered count, exterior color, footprint and capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a compliant, removable tongue cut into the insertion edge converts slot resistance into elastic deflection and restoring force that seats and retains the partition.
openings.delta: Replaces a rigid insertion interface with controlled compliance; dimensional overlap does not establish that interference caused the observed retries.
openings.prediction: Matched compliant samples require fewer retries and lower peak insertion force while retaining loaded stability and repeated removability.
openings.probe: Use six modified and six unchanged samples, holding board and slot dimensions comparable. Measure force, retries, loaded stability and repeated rearrangement damage; cost and time any template change before adoption.
assumptions: Failure boundary: board creasing, tearing or creep dissipates restoring force; orientation errors may receive no benefit.
Preserve footprint, stationery capacity, selected counts and exterior colors without permanent bonds; reject adoption if costs or preparation threaten the fixed delivery date.
